quotes.text: This is why Graph Data Connect exists. It's not a replacement for the Graph API. It's a completely different tool for a different job.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clarifies the positioning of Data Connect versus the Graph API.

quotes.text: The Graph API handles a real time access to small amounts of data while Data Connect is built for bulk extraction at massive scale.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A one-sentence comparison of the two access models.

quotes.text: Every pipeline run has about a 45 minute overhead before the data starts moving. So it's not for real-time dashboards. It's for scheduled, large-scale analytics that run nightly or weekly.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Names the key trade-off to plan for.

quotes.text: If you need a real-time alert when a file changes, use Power Automate. If you need to analyze usage patterns across all your SharePoint sites every night, use Graph Data Connect.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A concrete rule for picking the right tool.

quotes.text: Before you roll out Microsoft Copilot, you need to understand your data estate. Where does your data live? How is it organized? What permissions are in place? Data Connect can give you that inventory.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Connects bulk data extraction to Copilot readiness.

chapters.title: Intro: pulling M365 data out at scale
The scale problem with M365 data

takeaways: Microsoft Graph Data Connect is built for scheduled bulk extraction of Microsoft 365 data, while the Graph API serves real-time access to small amounts of data.
Admin consent, property-level scoping, encryption, identity obfuscation and audit trails make the bulk export suitable for regulated industries.
Data lands as Parquet files in a Fabric lakehouse or Azure storage, but the roughly 45-minute pipeline overhead and per-object pricing make it unsuitable for real-time scenarios.
hook: Pulling millions of Microsoft 365 records through the Graph API means throttling, pagination and endless retries. This episode explains Microsoft Graph Data Connect for admins, data engineers and analysts: how it differs from the Graph API, how it keeps data secure, where the data lands and how to set it up for large-scale analytics.
